claims.text: Drones travelling faster than 100mph (161km/h) lost their Starlink connection in Ukraine.
claims.explanation: Both sources report that Ukrainian drones lost their Starlink/Starshield connection at high speeds. Source 1 gives the 100 mph (160 km/h) threshold directly. Source 2 reports drops at speeds as low as 40 mph, which is consistent with drones above 100 mph also losing connection.

sources.title: Ukraine's drones lose their Starlink link above 100 mph. ...
sources.evidence: Ukrainian military users found that satellite-connected hardware traveling faster than 100 mph (160 km/h) lost its connection.

sources.title: When Starshield Cut Out, Ukrainian Drones Fell From the ...
sources.evidence: The initial Starshield throttling caused Ukrainian drones to lose their connection to the system when flying at speeds as low as 40 miles an hour.

claims.text: Starshield is controlled by the US military.
claims.explanation: Both sources report the statement that Starshield is controlled by the US government. Source 2 also says the US military decides limits on its use. Source 1 says only "US government", which is close enough to support the claim.

claims.text: Andy Burnham is the British prime minister.
claims.explanation: Both sources point to Andy Burnham as Prime Minister. The Wikipedia text says so directly. The gov.uk page lists the Prime Minister role on his official profile and says he became Labour leader in July 2026.

sources.title: Andy Burnham
sources.evidence: British politician who has served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Labour Party since July 2026.

sources.title: The Rt Hon Andy Burnham MP
sources.evidence: The gov.uk page for The Rt Hon Andy Burnham MP lists the Prime Minister role and says he was elected Leader of the Labour Party on 16 July 2026.

claims.text: Russia is not authorised to use the Starlink network.
claims.explanation: Neither source says whether Russia is officially authorised to use Starlink. Source 1 says Russia is building its own alternative. Source 2 says Russian forces were using Starlink terminals, which is about actual use and not about authorisation.

sources.title: Russia's Starlink substitute poses a security threat far ...
sources.evidence: Russia is currently developing a satellite network project meant to serve as a domestic alternative to SpaceX's Starlink.

sources.title: Starlink in the Russo-Ukrainian war
sources.evidence: Russian forces were reported by the Wall Street Journal to still be using Starlink terminals both in Ukraine and abroad in April 2024.
